title: Palestinian Gunman Kills Israeli Father of Six at Spring Near Neve Tzuf on Eve of Yom Kippur; Suspect Arrested
detail: A suspected Palestinian gunman opened fire from a vehicle on Israelis gathered at a natural spring near the Neve Tzuf (Halamish) settlement in the Ramallah area on Sunday, September 20, 2026, the eve of Yom Kippur, killing Netanel Shukrun, 46 (also reported as father of six from Alei Zahav settlement), who had gone to immerse in the spring with his eldest son. Shukrun, a systems information analyst whose wife Meirav lectures at Ariel University, died of his wounds in hospital shortly after. The gunman, a 37-year-old resident of Bidu village near Jerusalem, fled on foot; Israeli commandos arrested him unarmed at a Ramallah-area hospital roughly three hours later and recovered the weapon. Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan said Shukrun was 'a man of kindness, humble and a lover of people ... murdered just after he finished immersing with his son ahead of Yom Kippur.' National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir demanded the attacker be executed under Israel's March 2026 death-penalty law for Palestinians convicted of deadly attacks. Prime Minister Netanyahu said he had instructed security agencies to increase their presence and carry out arrests and offensive operations in the area; the IDF announced brigade-level raids, village closures around Ramallah and a planned home demolition, and said 27 battalion-equivalents are now deployed across the West Bank. Hamas praised the attack but denied responsibility.

title: IDF Kills Palestinian Driver in Thwarted Car-Ramming Attack Near West Bank Checkpoint by Ganim, Jenin
detail: Less than an hour after the Neve Tzuf spring shooting, Israeli soldiers shot and killed a Palestinian motorist near a checkpoint in the Ganim area of the Menashe Brigade's sector, near Jenin in the northern West Bank, on Sunday, September 20, 2026. The IDF said the driver attempted to ram troops stationed at the checkpoint; one attacker was killed and a second person in the vehicle was arrested. No soldiers were injured. It was not immediately clear whether the incident was coordinated with the Neve Tzuf shooting. Netanyahu said he had ordered security forces to increase their presence and conduct arrests and offensive operations across the West Bank following both incidents, which occurred on the eve of Yom Kippur.
